messages.subject: Bayesian exponentially tilted empirical likelihood
parts:
Another example (so I don't forget) about how cool it would be if Stan could define transformed / local parameters as solutions to optimization problems is this paper

http://scholar.google.com/scholar?cluster=11950043674090400861&hl=en&as_sdt=5,33&sciodt=0,33

which is another Bayesian nonparametric thing. Now that BFGS is fully operational, it seems like we wouldn't be too far from being able to solve the maximization problem in equation 10 to solve for the weights into equation 9 and then evaluate the posterior in equation 4. In other words, we mostly just need the Stan syntax, and then Stan can win a Nobel prize.

Ben
